quiz_item.question: What are the 'No-Zones' around a commercial tractor-trailer on the highway, and how should passenger vehicle drivers behave around them?
options: A. Designated highway rest areas where commercial truck drivers are prohibited from parking overnight.
B. Weigh-station bypass lanes where passenger cars can draft closely behind a trailer to save fuel.
C. Loading dock aprons where forklifts operate without backup alarms.

D. Large blind spots directly in front of the cab, directly behind the trailer, and along both sides (especially the wide right side) where the truck driver cannot see your car; never linger in these zones.

B. Weigh-station bypass lanes where passenger cars can draft closely behind a trailer to save fuel.

options: A. Diesel engines use two spark plugs per cylinder instead of one
B. Gasoline engines rely on compression heat alone while diesel engines use electric glow sparks
C. Diesel engines use high-pressure air compression heat to ignite fuel without spark plugs
D. Diesel engines burn fuel outside the cylinder before pushing pistons
choices: A. Diesel engines use two spark plugs per cylinder instead of one
B. Gasoline engines rely on compression heat alone while diesel engines use electric glow sparks
C. Diesel engines use high-pressure air compression heat to ignite fuel without spark plugs

quiz_item.correct_answer: C. Diesel engines use high-pressure air compression heat to ignite fuel without spark plugs
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (C): Unlike gasoline engines that ignite an air-fuel mix with a spark plug, diesel engines compress air to extreme pressures and temperatures before injecting fuel, which ignites spontaneously (p. 31).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: What are the 'No-Zones' around a commercial tractor-trailer on the highway, and how should passenger vehicle drivers behave around them?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: What are the 'No-Zones' around a commercial tractor-trailer on the highway, and how should passenger vehicle drivers behave around them?
options: A. Designated highway rest areas where commercial truck drivers are prohibited from parking overnight.
B. Weigh-station bypass lanes where passenger cars can draft closely behind a trailer to save fuel.
C. Loading dock aprons where forklifts operate without backup alarms.

D. Large blind spots directly in front of the cab, directly behind the trailer, and along both sides (especially the wide right side) where the truck driver cannot see your car; never linger in these zones.
choices: A. Designated highway rest areas where commercial truck drivers are prohibited from parking overnight.
B. Weigh-station bypass lanes where passenger cars can draft closely behind a trailer to save fuel.
C. Loading dock aprons where forklifts operate without backup alarms.

D. Large blind spots directly in front of the cab, directly behind the trailer, and along both sides (especially the wide right side) where the truck driver cannot see your car; never linger in these zones.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: D. Large blind spots directly in front of the cab, directly behind the trailer, and along both sides (especially the wide right side) where the truck driver cannot see your car; never linger in these zones.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (D): Tractor-trailers have large blind spots ('No-Zones') on both sides, closely in front, and up to 200 feet behind the trailer; if you cannot see the truck driver in their side mirror, the driver cannot see you.

options: A. Trucks haul raw materials to factories, move finished goods to warehouses, and deliver inventory to retailers
B. Trucks only move goods from warehouses to consumers' homes
C. Ocean liners deliver directly to regional warehouses, and trucks only handle damaged returns
D. Freight trains deliver raw materials directly to retail store loading docks
choices: A. Trucks haul raw materials to factories, move finished goods to warehouses, and deliver inventory to retailers
B. Trucks only move goods from warehouses to consumers' homes
C. Ocean liners deliver directly to regional warehouses, and trucks only handle damaged returns
D. Freight trains deliver raw materials directly to retail store loading docks
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: A. Trucks haul raw materials to factories, move finished goods to warehouses, and deliver inventory to retailers
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (A): Trucks provide the vital links at every stage of the supply chain, carrying raw materials to factories, finished products to storage warehouses, and retail stock to store shelves (p. 16).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: How does fuel ignition in a diesel truck engine differ from ignition in a gasoline engine?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: How does fuel ignition in a diesel truck engine differ from ignition in a gasoline engine?
options: A. Diesel engines use two spark plugs per cylinder instead of one
B. Gasoline engines rely on compression heat alone while diesel engines use electric glow sparks
C. Diesel engines use high-pressure air compression heat to ignite fuel without spark plugs
D. Diesel engines burn fuel outside the cylinder before pushing pistons
choices: A. Diesel engines use two spark plugs per cylinder instead of one
B. Gasoline engines rely on compression heat alone while diesel engines use electric glow sparks
C. Diesel engines use high-pressure air compression heat to ignite fuel without spark plugs
D. Diesel engines burn fuel outside the cylinder before pushing pistons
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: C. Diesel engines use high-pressure air compression heat to ignite fuel without spark plugs
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): Unlike gasoline engines that ignite an air-fuel mix with a spark plug, diesel engines compress air to extreme pressures and temperatures before injecting fuel, which ignites spontaneously (p. 31).
